target_customer: Casual sports fans, mostly people who had never played daily fantasy sports, playing free contests for prizes
problem: Daily fantasy sports sites were complex for casual fans. Gameday offered simpler contests inside a Facebook Messenger chatbot.
business_model: Free to play with in-app currency redeemable for prizes, monetization not stated
product_category: Daily fantasy sports chatbot on Facebook Messenger

founders.name: LC Carrier
founders.background_notes: The YC page lists LC Carrier as Founder, shown twice, with no education or employers. Search snippets from Crunchbase also named Thierry Skoda as CTO, but that page was not opened, so he is not listed.

competitors.name: FanDuel
competitors.what: Daily fantasy sports operator that had just launched a lite version for casual users

technical_complexity.rationale: A Messenger chatbot with contest rules and lineup entry is modest engineering, with the main dependence on Facebook platform features.

defensibility.rationale: Simple contests on a public platform could be copied quickly, and theScore launched a similar Messenger game within months.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: FanDuel launched a lite product for casual fans. theScore launched a Messenger fantasy game in early 2018. Gameday is listed inactive.

market_need_then: TechCrunch in August 2017 reported about 25,000 daily players before the NHL season ended, with about 75% never having played daily fantasy before.

identity.voice_and_tone: Pitched as the easiest way to play fantasy sports with friends

brand_strength.rationale: No brand coverage found beyond product coverage, and the generic name is shared with unrelated sports products.

outcome_analysis: Gameday launched in Summer 2017 as a free daily fantasy game inside Facebook Messenger and reported about 25,000 daily players. It depended on Messenger features, notably group chat support that was planned but not available, and FanDuel and theScore moved into the same casual space. The company is now inactive and the cause is not public, so these two factors are inferred from the launch coverage rather than stated by the founders.
notes: No company website is listed in the directory, so the site is treated as dead. Crunchbase shows a Seed Round label with no amount or date in the snippet seen; Dealroom shows an enterprise value of $2M, which is a valuation estimate and not a raise. The seed round rests on a single database label. The theScore Messenger game launched in early 2018 and is not listed as a competitor at founding.
